raw_response:
I'm 66 years old. My back isn't what it was, but this land is all I have. My father grew wheat and corn on this ground, and his father before him. Quzhou soil is good flat land — North China Plain. I know what this land wants.

I have about 5 mu I can still manage myself, though my son helps during harvest. I won't try anything new — new seeds from strangers fail, and I cannot afford a bad year. The extension station pushed cotton on us twenty years ago and half the village lost money. I grow what I know.

**Winter wheat** goes in October when the soil cools, same as always. I buy the improved wheat seed from the township supply co-op — not the fancy hybrid stuff, but the improved variety the neighbors use, "Shi 4185" or whatever they're selling this year. I fertilize before sowing with a bag of compound fertilizer, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: when I sow, before winter freeze, at jointing, and at grain filling. In Quzhou the ground water is still reachable. Spray once for aphids, once for rust if I see it.

**Summer maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use the Zhengdan 958 hybrid kernel because that's what the village seed shop has and everyone around me uses it. I scatter urea twice — once after emergence, once at tasseling. Summer rains help but I'll pump once if July is dry. Spray for corn borer once.

I won't change what works. I'm too old to experiment and too poor to fail.
